# Implementation Plan: task-phases — Phase-aware status model for codexu roadmap dashboard

*Generated by `/plan-with-ralph` on 2026-05-17. Ready for `/implement-with-ralph --from-plan .ralph/jobs/task-phases/plan.md`.*

## Overview

Today the codexu bookkeeping convention tracks one row per task in `plans/overview.html` and `plans/parallel-assignments.md`, with a single status badge (`b-ready`/`b-blocked`/`b-paused`/`b-closed`/`b-inprogress`) collapsing three distinct operator actions (brainstorm / plan / implement) plus three different intermediate review-pause states. This makes it impossible to tell from the dashboard whether a "ready" task has a plan landed-but-unreviewed, a plan-approved-but-impl-not-started, or no plan at all — they all collapse to `b-ready`.

This plan introduces a **phase-aware status model** as the HTML-only change surface. Every task carries an explicit `phase` (the 10-value enum `brainstorm-ready | brainstorm-in-progress | brainstorm-review | plan-ready | plan-in-progress | plan-review | impl-ready | impl-in-progress | shipped | closed`) plus a separate cross-cutting `status` modifier (`ok | blocked | paused`), expressed as `data-task-phase` and `data-task-status` HTML attributes on every `<details class="cmd">` row. CSS badges and JS classifiers/filters/Today-panel logic all read from these attributes, with legacy `.b-*` classes preserved as fail-soft aliases. This is plan #1 of three sibling plans that already exist as drafts in `plans/`: `overview-data-split.md` (extracts the data into a sidecar file) and `overview-vite-react.md` (rewrites the viewer as a Vite/React app) both reference this plan's phase enum and `planSource` model and are explicitly blocked on it landing first.

### Technical Constraints

- **HTML-only.** No build step, no Vite, no React, no sidecar JSON extraction (the last is plan #2's scope). The phase schema must be representable in static HTML.
- **The JS reads status from CSS classes today.** If we only change badge classes, sorting/filters/Today-panel/section-counts will silently drift. The right shape (per Codex research and operator confirmation) is to make `data-task-phase` and `data-task-status` HTML attributes the source of truth, with badge classes being derived render artifacts.
- **Backwards-compat for legacy `b-*` classes.** A future hand-edited task that accidentally uses `b-ready` / `b-blocked` / `b-paused` / `b-closed` / `b-inprogress` must render something readable rather than blank. Either keep the legacy classes aliased to nearest new phase (default `plan-ready` for `b-ready`, etc.) or fail-soft to a default style.
- **Dark/light theme parity.** Light theme `@media` block has the same token set as dark (`--bg --fg --muted --border --card --card-hover --accent --ok --warn --bad --info --done --purple`). New phase classes must work in both themes.
- **Phase is operator-asserted, never inferred from filesystem state.** The presence of `.ralph/jobs/<task-id>/plan.md` is NOT a reliable phase signal — operator-judgment is required for `plan-review` vs `plan-ready`, and for `brainstorm-ready` vs `plan-ready`.
- **TypeScript-friendly schema design (per architect recommendation, to de-risk plans #2 / #3).** Lock in NOW: standardize absent optional fields to `null` (not `undefined`); make `phase` required with default `plan-ready` for un-fired concrete tasks; treat `planSource` as explicit required enum once `planPrompt` is present.

## Approach

### Architecture

**Two-layer model:**

1. **Authoritative layer — HTML data attributes.** Every `<details class="cmd">` row carries:
   - `data-task-phase="<one-of-10-enum-values>"` (required, default `plan-ready`)
   - `data-task-status="ok|blocked|paused"` (required, default `ok`)
   - Optional artifact/source attributes (all omit-when-absent rather than `null`-attribute, to keep HTML readable):
     - `data-plan-only` (boolean — presence-flag)
     - `data-plan-source="fresh|from-brainstorm|from-plan-doc"`
     - `data-plan-source-ref="<relative path>"` (only for `from-plan-doc`)
     - `data-brainstorm-job-id="<id>"`
     - `data-plan-job-id="<id>"`
     - `data-implement-job-id="<id>"`
     - `data-plan-review-iterations="<int>"` (only when > 0)
     - `data-merge-commit="<sha>"` (only when `phase === "shipped"`)
   - Prompt strings (`brainstormPrompt`, `planPrompt`, `implementPrompt`) stay where they live today — inside the `<pre class="cmd-pre">` body — because they are already rendered prose and don't fit cleanly into attributes. The schema doesn't introduce new fields for them in this plan; they remain prose content that operators read.
2. **Render layer — CSS badge classes derived from data attributes by a render IIFE.** The visible badge in `<summary>` is rendered by:
   - A primary phase pill `.cmd-badge.b-<phase>` (e.g., `.b-plan-ready`, `.b-impl-in-progress`)
   - A secondary smaller status modifier pill `<span class="cmd-status-mod">blocked</span>` rendered alongside the primary when `data-task-status !== "ok"`
   - **`data-task-phase` is the single source of truth — the visible badge is a render artifact.** A new `renderPhaseBadges()` IIFE near the top of the existing `<script>` block (just after `injectTaskScopeChips()` at `2626-2668`) walks every `<details class="cmd">[data-task-phase]`, normalizes the inline `.cmd-badge` element's class to `cmd-badge b-<data-task-phase>` (replacing any stale legacy `b-*` class), and inserts/removes the inline `<span class="cmd-status-mod">` sub-badge based on `data-task-status`. Bookkeepers only edit attributes; the IIFE flips classes on page load. Rows that carry ONLY a legacy `b-*` class without `data-task-phase` are derived-in-reverse by the IIFE (it populates `data-task-phase` from the legacy class via the inverse of `PHASE_TO_FILTER_BUCKET`) so they canonicalize at runtime. **No bookkeeper dual-write is required** — risk #5 (badge-class / attribute drift) is eliminated because the class becomes a function of the attribute, not a parallel hand-edit.
   - **Color palette per phase family**, mapping to existing CSS vars: brainstorm-phase → `--purple` (3 intensities ready/in-progress/review via opacity or saturation), plan-phase → `--info` / `--accent`, impl-phase → `--warn`, `shipped` → `--ok`, `closed` → `--done`. Status-modifier pill: `--warn` for `blocked`, `--muted` for `paused`.

**JS reads attributes, not classes.** `classifyAndOrderCmds()`, `classifyCmd()`, the multi-axis filter, and the Today panel all switch to reading `data-task-phase` / `data-task-status`. **Two parallel mappings are required** because order and filter consumers treat `shipped` vs `closed` differently:

- `PHASE_TO_ORDER_BUCKET` (consumed by `classifyAndOrderCmds()` at `2671-2695`, where `shipped` sorts separately from `closed` per existing behavior captured in commit `b2598368`): `brainstorm-*` → `brainstorm`, `plan-*`/`impl-ready` → `ready`, `impl-in-progress` → `inprogress`, `shipped` → `shipped`, `closed` → `closed`.
- `PHASE_TO_FILTER_BUCKET` (consumed by `classifyCmd()` at `2842-2851`, the multi-axis filter at `3126-3163`, and the Today panel at `962` — where `shipped` and `closed` collapse into a single bucket as today): same mapping as ORDER_BUCKET except `shipped` → `closed` and `closed` → `closed`.

Both constants live near the top of the existing `<script>` block. Existing UX (3-column kanban, Today panel categories, filter chip labels) is preserved on day one. The toolbar `Status` filter chips at `978-985` stay labelled as today; phase becomes filterable via a new axis introduced as **out of scope for v1** (the chips themselves are not changed in this plan — see "Out of scope").

**Precedence rule — status modifier vs phase.** Both `data-task-phase` and `data-task-status` map to legacy buckets, and a single row can carry e.g. `data-task-phase="plan-ready"` + `data-task-status="blocked"`. To resolve which bucket wins per consumer:

- **Filter and Today-panel bucket assignment (`classifyCmd()`, the multi-axis filter, the Today-panel grouping at line `962`):** the status modifier takes precedence over phase. A row with `data-task-status="blocked"` classifies into the `blocked` bucket regardless of phase; `data-task-status="paused"` classifies into the `paused` bucket regardless of phase; `data-task-status="ok"` falls through to `PHASE_TO_FILTER_BUCKET`. Concretely, for `data-task-phase="plan-ready"` + `data-task-status="blocked"`, `classifyCmd()` returns `"blocked"` (not `"ready"`).
- **Sort/order bucket assignment (`classifyAndOrderCmds()` at `2671-2695`):** phase only via `PHASE_TO_ORDER_BUCKET`. The status modifier never affects sort order. Rows are ordered by phase (with `shipped` sorted separately from `closed`, preserving today's behavior per recent commit `b2598368`); a `plan-ready` + `blocked` row sorts in the same bucket as a `plan-ready` + `ok` row.
- **Kanban columns** are not re-assigned in this plan. Cards stay in the column they are manually placed in inside the existing static HTML (`1061-1395` within `sec-kanban` opening at `1043`). The code at `2953-2965` is `populateKanbanCount` — it only **counts** existing `.card` elements per `.kanban .col` to render the section's collapsed-summary count badge. No phase-derived column placement is introduced; the per-card phase **pill** added in Implementation Strategy step 5 is purely visual and does not move cards between columns.

This precedence is documented as a code comment above the `PHASE_TO_ORDER_BUCKET` and `PHASE_TO_FILTER_BUCKET` constants and at the top of each consumer function so future edits don't accidentally re-derive the bucket from phase alone.

**Legacy class aliasing for fail-soft.** If a future task entry uses only a legacy `.b-ready` / `.b-blocked` / etc. class without `data-task-phase`, the JS falls back to the legacy class mapping (the same rules today's code uses). CSS keeps the legacy classes styled, equivalently to today, so the dashboard renders cleanly even if a bookkeeper forgets the new attributes.

### Implementation Strategy

Execution order (each step is a self-contained commit if helpful):

1. **CSS first.** Add the 10 new `.cmd-badge.b-<phase>` classes and the `.cmd-status-mod` sub-badge to `plans/overview.html` near the existing badge block at lines `845-849`. Wire colors through existing semantic CSS vars; verify both `@media` color schemes. Existing legacy `.b-ready` / `.b-blocked` / `.b-paused` / `.b-closed` / `.b-inprogress` are NOT removed — they stay as fail-soft aliases.
2. **JS reader plumbing + render-from-attribute IIFE.** Update `classifyAndOrderCmds()` (`2671-2695`) to read `data-task-phase` via `PHASE_TO_ORDER_BUCKET`. Update `classifyCmd()` (`2842-2851`), the multi-axis filter (`3126-3163`), and any Today-panel bucket logic at `962` to read `data-task-status` first (with status precedence) then `data-task-phase` via `PHASE_TO_FILTER_BUCKET`. Both consumers fall back to the legacy class mapping when the attributes are missing. Introduce **two** `PHASE_TO_ORDER_BUCKET` and `PHASE_TO_FILTER_BUCKET` constants near the top of the script block (see Architecture > "JS reads attributes" above for the exact mappings). **The 2953-2965 `populateKanbanCount` IIFE requires no change** — it counts cards per existing column, not by phase. **Add a new `renderPhaseBadges()` IIFE** (place it just after `injectTaskScopeChips()` at `2626-2668`) that, on page load: (a) for every `<details class="cmd">[data-task-phase]`, normalizes the inline primary `.cmd-badge` element's class to `cmd-badge b-<data-task-phase>` (replacing any stale legacy `b-*` class found inside the badge's `classList`); (b) inserts or removes the `<span class="cmd-status-mod">` sub-badge based on `data-task-status` (insert as the next-sibling of `.cmd-badge` when status is `blocked` or `paused`, remove otherwise); (c) for rows that carry ONLY a legacy `b-*` class and no `data-task-phase`, derives `data-task-phase` from the legacy class via the inverse of `PHASE_TO_FILTER_BUCKET` (default: `plan-ready` for `b-ready`, `impl-in-progress` for `b-inprogress`, `closed` for `b-closed`) and applies normalization. **Also update `injectTaskScopeChips()` at `2626-2668`** to relocate the new `.cmd-status-mod` sub-badge into the `.cmd-scope-cluster` wrapper alongside `.cmd-badge` — today the injector only moves `.cmd-badge` (line `2644`, appended last at line `2667`); without this change a newly rendered `.cmd-status-mod` written next to the primary badge in `<summary>` will be left OUTSIDE the cluster, breaking the "secondary badge next to primary" visual group. Capture both elements before building the cluster, then append `.cmd-badge` followed by `.cmd-status-mod` last so the modifier sits immediately to the right of the phase badge. **Order of IIFE invocation:** `renderPhaseBadges()` MUST run before `injectTaskScopeChips()` so the modifier exists when the cluster is built.
3. **Migrate all 49 command rows.** Add `data-task-phase` and `data-task-status` attributes to every `<details class="cmd">`. **Because `renderPhaseBadges()` normalizes the visible badge class from the attribute on load, the legacy `cmd-badge b-<status>` class may be left as-is during migration** — the IIFE will flip it to `cmd-badge b-<phase>` at runtime. Bookkeepers MAY pre-flip the class to match (cosmetic only — the view-source HTML stays readable), but this is optional. Add the optional artifact attributes (`data-plan-only`, `data-plan-source`, `data-plan-source-ref`, `data-{brainstorm,plan,implement}-job-id`, `data-merge-commit`) where they apply. **Use the pinned "Migration Mapping" table below as the authoritative per-row assignment** — no operator clarification is required to run autonomously. Status-modifier `<span class="cmd-status-mod">` sub-badges do NOT need to be pre-inserted in the HTML; `renderPhaseBadges()` injects/removes them based on `data-task-status` at load time.
4. **Reconcile drift.** As part of step 3, fix the known drift on `perf-WS3` and `1a-fork-doc` so `overview.html` and `parallel-assignments.md` agree on their phase. The single-source-of-truth here is the actual current state in the repo (commits landed → `shipped`; not landed → use operator judgment).
5. **Kanban-card phase pills.** Cards at `1061-1395` (within the `sec-kanban` section that opens at `1043`) get a small phase pill via `data-task-id` matching against command rows (more robust than the existing brittle title-text match). Add `data-task-id` on each kanban card; the JS reads it to look up the command row's `data-task-phase` and injects a phase pill. **Refactor BOTH existing title-text matchers to consume the new `data-task-id` attribute:** (a) the workstream-tagging IIFE at `3293-3307` (the kanban half of the `linkWorkstreams` block — "tag data-workstream for filtering by name matching"), and (b) the `linkKanbanToCmds` IIFE at `3334-3355` (cross-section `→ command` jump-link injection). Both currently substring-match `title.textContent`; both should read `card.dataset.taskId` directly. The single new `data-task-id` attribute on each kanban card supports all three consumers (phase-pill injection, workstream tagging, `→ command` link injection).

Extend the per-task status table (`553-583+`) to include explicit phase and status columns (replace the existing single `Status` column with `Phase | Status | Plan source | Plan job`).

## Migration Mapping

Authoritative phase + status assignment for all 49 command rows. Derived deterministically from the current badge + repo state per the rules in `plans/task-phases.md` "Schema mapping for existing tasks". An autonomous `/implement-with-ralph` run uses this table as-is; no operator clarification required. Tasks flagged `TBD` are the small set the source doc explicitly leaves to operator judgment — for those, the table records a safe default plus the alternative, and the implementer applies the default unless an operator override is provided at run time.

Mapping rules applied:
- `b-closed` with ✅ shipped → `phase: shipped`, `status: ok`
- `b-closed` with 🚫 closed → `phase: closed`, `status: ok`

- `b-blocked` → `phase: plan-ready`, `status: blocked` (un-fired tasks; preserve phase = default `plan-ready`)
- `b-paused` → `phase: plan-ready`, `status: paused` (same)
- Research/docs tasks with terminal `shipped` doc → also `data-plan-only` presence-flag set

## Scope

### In Scope

- Phase enum + status modifier as HTML `data-*` attributes on every command row
- New CSS badge classes (10 phase classes + 1 modifier class) with dark/light theme parity
- JS classifier / filter / kanban-column / Today-panel updates to read from data attributes (with legacy-class fallback)
- Migration of all 49 existing command rows + every kanban card per the pinned "Migration Mapping" table
- Reconciliation of `perf-WS3` and `1a-fork-doc` drift between `overview.html` and `parallel-assignments.md`
- Documentation updates in `parallel-assignments.md` (front-matter + per-task table), `codexu-roadmap.md` (Standing rules), and `.agents/skills/roadmap-and-overview/SKILL.md`
- Legacy `b-*` class fail-soft aliasing (do not remove)
- Lock in field names and enum values for forward-compatibility with plans #2 and #3 (which already reference this plan's phase enum and `planSource` model). TypeScript-level null-vs-undefined handling for persisted JSON is plan #2's (`overview-data-split.md`) concern, not this HTML-only plan's.
- Manual smoke of all 4 progression paths using pinned targets (`agent-comms` brainstorm / `1b-multidev` standard / `codex-claude-md-autoload` fused / `codex-parity-audit` planOnly)

### Out of Scope

- Extracting task data out of HTML into a sidecar JSON/JS file — that is `overview-data-split.md` (plan #2)
- Rewriting the viewer as Vite + React — that is `overview-vite-react.md` (plan #3)
- Any inline-edit affordance to change phase from the UI — earliest is `overview-vite-react.md` Stage 6.5
- Auto-bumping `lastTouchedAt` in `roadmap-data` JSON when phase changes — bookkeeper bumps manually
- New kanban columns — preserve the 3-column structure (`Ready` / `Soon` / `Blocked`); phase becomes a pill on each card
- Adding a `Phase` filter chip to the toolbar at `978-985` (the existing `Status` chips stay as-is; phase is filterable in v1 only via deep-linking / text search). Adding a phase axis is a follow-up.
- Auto-populating `data-*-job-id` artifact attributes from filesystem state — bookkeeper populates manually after each operator action
- Auto-deriving `phase === "plan-review"` from the existence of `.ralph/jobs/<task-id>/plan.md` — operator-asserted only
- Touching `.ralph/jobs/*/plan.md` files (per-task PRDs)
- Touching the existing roadmap phase tree at `1895+` (it's a different "phase" concept — workstream phases, not task phases)
- Adding `phaseTreePath` (this is plan #2's field)
- A `Phase | Modifier | Plan source/job | Commit` super-detailed status table format in `parallel-assignments.md` — keep it to `Phase | Status | Plan source | Plan job` as the v1 schema (Commit column stays where it is today)

## Risk Areas

1. **JS classifier regression.** Updating `classifyAndOrderCmds()`, `classifyCmd()`, and the multi-axis filter at the same time risks breaking the Today panel, the section ordering, or the kanban summary count. Mitigation: introduce the two `PHASE_TO_ORDER_BUCKET` + `PHASE_TO_FILTER_BUCKET` constants and reuse them across the four call sites; ensure every legacy bucket name maps from at least one phase value in each direction; smoke each progression path in a browser using the temporary-copy procedure in Acceptance Criteria.
2. **CSS specificity collision** between new `.cmd-badge.b-<phase>` and existing `.b-ready` etc. The same rule should style both; legacy classes must not override the new phase class when both are present (bookkeeper transition state). Mitigation: do not use `!important` on legacy classes; rely on CSS document order with new classes after the legacy block; if collision found in QA, scope new classes via a wrapper class `.cmd-badge.b-phase` to bump specificity.
3. **Light-theme readability.** New phase colors must work in both themes. The light theme defines all the same tokens (no missing), so reuse is safe — but the brainstorm-phase 3 intensities (via opacity or saturation) need visual QA in light mode where the `--purple` base color may render differently.
4. **Migration mismatch.** Operator-asserted phase for 49 rows is error-prone. Mitigation: the pinned "Migration Mapping" table above gives every row a deterministic default derived from current badge state; only `agent-comms` carries a TBD operator override (brainstorm-ready vs plan-ready+blocked) and the table records a safe default for autonomous execution.
5. **`renderPhaseBadges()` IIFE failures.** If the render IIFE throws or fails to run (e.g., a missing `.cmd-badge` inside a row), the visible badge will be stale (legacy `b-*` class) until a page reload after the fix. Mitigation: wrap the per-row body in `try {} catch {}` so one bad row does not abort the whole pass; log the failed `data-task-id` to `console.warn` so operators can debug; the dashboard still renders (just with the wrong color on the failed row).
6. **Sibling-plan enum lock-in.** Plans #2 and #3 already reference the enum values and field names. Any rename forces a follow-up edit to both sibling docs. Mitigation: lock in field names from the source doc verbatim (`phase`, `status`, `planSource`, `brainstormJobId`, `planJobId`, `implementJobId`, `mergeCommit`, `planReviewIterations`, `planOnly`, `brainstormPrompt`, `planPrompt`, `implementPrompt`); update siblings ONLY if their references are inconsistent with the source doc.
7. **`pill-spawned-from` visual collision with new phase pills.** Both render on the same task card. Mitigation: phase pill stays in `<summary>`; spawned-from pill stays in body (existing placement at `3436+`). Architect confirmed no positional clash.
8. **Kanban-card phase-pill injection brittleness.** The existing title-text matchers at `3293-3307` (workstream tagging) and `3334-3355` (`→ command` link injection) were the brittle baseline. Switching to `data-task-id` lookup is more robust but assumes every command row AND every kanban card has `data-task-id`. Verify all 49 command rows have it after migration; verify every kanban card has it; missing IDs default to "no phase pill / no workstream tag / no jump-link" rather than crash.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every one of the 49 `<details class="cmd">` data rows in `plans/overview.html` carries a valid `data-task-phase` (one of the 10 enum values) and `data-task-status` (one of `ok | blocked | paused`). Note: `grep -c '<details class="cmd"' plans/overview.html` returns 51 raw matches but only 49 are real data rows — line `851` is a docstring example inside a CSS comment and line `2799` is a JS comment that contains the same string. Verifiable via grep — all of the following must hold:
  - `grep -c 'data-task-phase="' plans/overview.html` returns **exactly 49**
  - `grep -c 'data-task-status="' plans/overview.html` returns **exactly 49**
  - The two counts are equal to each other (every row that carries one attribute carries the other)
  - Enum-value check (phase): `grep -oP 'data-task-phase="\K[^"]+' plans/overview.html | sort -u` returns **only** the 10 allowed phase values (`brainstorm-ready`, `brainstorm-in-progress`, `brainstorm-review`, `plan-ready`, `plan-in-progress`, `plan-review`, `impl-ready`, `impl-in-progress`, `shipped`, `closed`) — no extras, no typos
  - Enum-value check (status): `grep -oP 'data-task-status="\K[^"]+' plans/overview.html | sort -u` returns **only** `blocked`, `ok`, `paused` — no extras, no typos
- Per-row phase + status values match the pinned "Migration Mapping" table (each row's `data-task-phase` and `data-task-status` agree with the table entry for its `data-task-id`).
- Every one of the 49 rows carries a primary CSS phase badge (`.cmd-badge.b-<phase>`) whose suffix matches its `data-task-phase` value. **The badge class is rendered at load time by the `renderPhaseBadges()` IIFE from `data-task-phase`** (it normalizes stale legacy classes), so a verifier loads `plans/overview.html` in a browser and runs `document.querySelectorAll('details.cmd[data-task-phase]').forEach(d => { const want = 'b-' + d.dataset.taskPhase; const have = [...d.querySelector('.cmd-badge').classList].find(c => c.startsWith('b-')); console.assert(have === want, d.dataset.taskId, have, '!=', want); })` in DevTools console; zero assertion failures.
- Rows with `data-task-status !== "ok"` render a secondary `<span class="cmd-status-mod">` sub-badge next to the primary phase badge. Both the primary `.cmd-badge` and the secondary `.cmd-status-mod` sit inside the same `.cmd-scope-cluster` wrapper (relocated by the updated `injectTaskScopeChips()` injector at `2626-2668`), so they render as one tight visual group on the right of the summary row.
- The 10 new CSS classes are defined in `plans/overview.html` and render visually distinct colors in both the dark `:root` block (`7-21`) and the light `@media (prefers-color-scheme: light)` block (`22-38`). Verifiable via the following concrete checks:
  - **Class definition grep:** `grep -cE '\.cmd-badge\.b-(brainstorm-ready\|brainstorm-in-progress\|brainstorm-review\|plan-ready\|plan-in-progress\|plan-review\|impl-ready\|impl-in-progress\|shipped\|closed)' plans/overview.html` returns **at least 10** (each class is defined at least once in the CSS block).
  - **Status modifier class defined:** `grep -cE '\.cmd-status-mod' plans/overview.html` returns at least 1 (defined as a CSS class).
  - **Computed-style smoke (DevTools, both themes):** load `plans/overview.html` in a browser, run `['brainstorm-ready','brainstorm-in-progress','brainstorm-review','plan-ready','plan-in-progress','plan-review','impl-ready','impl-in-progress','shipped','closed'].forEach(p => { const el = document.createElement('span'); el.className = 'cmd-badge b-' + p; document.body.appendChild(el); const bg = getComputedStyle(el).backgroundColor; console.log(p, bg); el.remove(); })` in DevTools console; verify no value is `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)` / `transparent`, every value is non-empty, no two phases in the same phase-family (brainstorm, plan, impl) resolve to the identical color.
  - **Manual visual check:** toggle DevTools > Rendering > Emulate CSS media `prefers-color-scheme: light` and again with `dark`; visually confirm no phase badge is invisible or unreadable in either theme; capture pass/fail notes in the PR description.
- Legacy classes (`.b-ready`, `.b-blocked`, `.b-paused`, `.b-closed`, `.b-inprogress`) remain defined and render readably (no blank pills). A task row using ONLY a legacy class (no `data-task-phase`) renders correctly and is classified into the right legacy bucket by JS.
- `classifyAndOrderCmds()` reads `data-task-phase` via `PHASE_TO_ORDER_BUCKET` (shipped sorted separately from closed). `classifyCmd()`, the multi-axis filter, and the Today panel read `data-task-status` first (status precedence) then `data-task-phase` via `PHASE_TO_FILTER_BUCKET` (shipped collapsed into closed). All four consumers fall back to the legacy class mapping when attributes are missing. The toolbar `Status` filter chips at `978-985` continue to filter as today (e.g., clicking "ready" surfaces all `plan-ready`, `impl-ready`, `plan-review` rows mapped to the `ready` bucket via `PHASE_TO_FILTER_BUCKET`). The kanban static HTML and the `populateKanbanCount` IIFE at `2953-2965` are unchanged; cards stay in their manually-placed columns.
- **Precedence rule honored.** A row with `data-task-phase="plan-ready"` + `data-task-status="blocked"` is classified into the `blocked` bucket by `classifyCmd()`, the multi-axis filter, and the Today panel, but is ordered by `classifyAndOrderCmds()` using its phase only (sorts alongside other `plan-ready` rows, not into a separate sort bucket). The kanban static HTML is unaffected — cards do not move columns. Verifiable by inspecting at least one such row in the migration (e.g., `perf-WS2`, `3b-agents`, `agent-comms` — every `b-blocked` and `b-paused` row in the table) in the filter, Today-panel, and section-ordering surfaces.
- Every kanban card at `1061-1395` (within the `sec-kanban` section opening at `1043`) carries a `data-task-id`; cards display a phase pill that reflects their corresponding command row's `data-task-phase`. Both brittle title-text matchers — workstream tagging at `3293-3307` and `linkKanbanToCmds` (`→ command` link injection) at `3334-3355` — are refactored to read `card.dataset.taskId` instead of substring-matching `title.textContent`.
- `perf-WS3` and `1a-fork-doc` have consistent phase values in both `plans/overview.html` and `plans/parallel-assignments.md` (no drift).
- `plans/parallel-assignments.md` front-matter conventions block (`1-22`) documents the phase enum + status modifier + optional artifact field schema. The per-task status table (`553-583+`) carries explicit `Phase` and `Status` columns.
- `plans/codexu-roadmap.md` Standing rules section (`163-174`) carries a one-paragraph "Task phase model" entry linking to `plans/parallel-assignments.md`.
- `.agents/skills/roadmap-and-overview/SKILL.md` references the new phase + status model rather than the legacy `b-*`-only model. The procedural workflow (when to update what, etc.) is preserved.
- **Manual smoke of all 4 progression paths using the pinned targets on a temporary copy of `plans/overview.html`** (do NOT mutate the real dashboard). Procedure: `cp plans/overview.html plans/overview.smoke.html` (the `.smoke.html` suffix is ignored by `.gitignore`-equivalent — verify before starting; if not ignored, work on an out-of-tree path like `/tmp/overview.smoke.html` and load via `file://`). In the copy, walk these pinned targets through their full progression by editing `data-task-phase` (the `renderPhaseBadges()` IIFE auto-flips the badge class on reload):
  - **Brainstorm path:** `agent-comms` — flip `brainstorm-ready` → `brainstorm-in-progress` → `brainstorm-review` → `plan-ready`.
  - **Standard path:** `1b-multidev` — flip `plan-ready` → `plan-in-progress` → `plan-review` → `impl-ready` → `impl-in-progress` → `shipped`.
  - **Fused (1-paragraph plan + impl) path:** `codex-claude-md-autoload` — flip `plan-ready` → `impl-in-progress` → `shipped` (skipping `plan-in-progress`/`plan-review`/`impl-ready` per the fused convention).

  Reload the smoke copy in a browser between each transition; verify the badge color flips correctly, the filter chips classify the row as expected, the Today-panel buckets it correctly, and the section ordering moves the row appropriately. **Discard the smoke copy after the smoke is complete** (`rm plans/overview.smoke.html` or remove the out-of-tree copy). Capture pass/fail per target in the PR description with one line per transition.
- Backwards-compat smoke: a hand-crafted test row with only `<span class="cmd-badge b-ready">` (no `data-task-phase`) renders visually identical to today's `b-ready` rows and classifies into the `ready` bucket.
- Open `plans/overview.html` in both dark and light themes (toggle browser `prefers-color-scheme`); no visual regression in kanban, command rows, Today panel, filter chips, or the spawn-relationship pills.

## Preliminary Story Decomposition

1. **US-001: CSS + JS plumbing for phase + status schema.** Add the 10 new CSS phase classes + status modifier class (preserving dark/light theme tokens, legacy `.b-*` classes kept as aliases). Update `classifyAndOrderCmds()` (via `PHASE_TO_ORDER_BUCKET`), `classifyCmd()` and the multi-axis filter (via `PHASE_TO_FILTER_BUCKET` with status precedence) to read `data-task-phase` / `data-task-status` (fall back to legacy class). Introduce both `PHASE_TO_ORDER_BUCKET` and `PHASE_TO_FILTER_BUCKET` constants. Add `renderPhaseBadges()` IIFE that derives the visible badge class from `data-task-phase` on load (eliminates dual-write). Update `injectTaskScopeChips()` to relocate `.cmd-status-mod` into the scope cluster. Refactor kanban-card phase-pill injection from brittle title-text match to `data-task-id` lookup (incl. the second matcher in `linkKanbanToCmds` at `3334-3355`). **Estimated complexity:** medium.
2. **US-002: Migrate all 49 command rows + kanban cards.** Add `data-task-phase`, `data-task-status`, optional artifact attrs (`data-plan-only`, `data-plan-source`, `data-plan-source-ref`, `data-{brainstorm,plan,implement}-job-id`, `data-plan-review-iterations`, `data-merge-commit`) to every `<details class="cmd">` and matching kanban card. Update the visible primary badge class to match the new phase value. Render status-modifier sub-badges where applicable. **Per-row values are pinned in the "Migration Mapping" table above** — no operator confirmation required; apply the table verbatim. **Estimated complexity:** large (49 rows × ~3 attrs minimum each).
3. **US-003: Reconcile known drift.** Fix `perf-WS3` and `1a-fork-doc` phase values so `overview.html` and `parallel-assignments.md` agree. Both are pinned to `shipped` in the migration table. **Estimated complexity:** small.
4. **US-004: Docs updates.** Update `plans/parallel-assignments.md` (front-matter + per-task table), `plans/codexu-roadmap.md` (Standing rules), and `.agents/skills/roadmap-and-overview/SKILL.md` (replace legacy `b-*` references with phase + status). **Estimated complexity:** medium (SKILL.md updates touch multiple line ranges).
5. **US-005: Smoke test the 4 progression paths.** Walk the pinned representative tasks through each path: Brainstorm (`agent-comms`), Standard (`1b-multidev`), Fused 1-paragraph (`codex-claude-md-autoload`), planOnly (`codex-parity-audit`). Verify CSS rendering + JS classification + kanban placement + Today panel in both dark and light themes. Verify legacy-class fail-soft on a hand-crafted test row. For brainstorm and fused smoke targets, restore the canonical row to its pinned migration value before merging.
